import bands from "./bands.png";

# Figure layout

The same 540 × 180 raster appears in several layouts without page CSS.

## Image in a figure

<figure class="fig" id="single">
<img src={bands} alt="Three blue bands" />
<figcaption>A direct child of a figure with the fig class.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure class="fig" id="sized">
<img src={bands} width="540" height="180" alt="Three blue bands" />
<figcaption>A direct child with width and height attributes.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Two plain figures in a split

<div class="split fig" id="pair">
<figure>
<img src={bands} alt="Three blue bands" />
<figcaption>First column.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure>
<img src={bands} alt="Three blue bands" />
<figcaption>Second column.</figcaption>
</figure>
</div>

## Plain figure in prose

The figure below keeps the usual spacing in prose.

<figure id="prose-figure">
<img src={bands} width="540" height="180" alt="Three blue bands" />
<figcaption>A plain figure outside the split.</figcaption>
</figure>

The paragraph after the figure.

## Image beside prose

<div class="beside">
<p>On a wide screen the figure stays beside the prose.</p>
<figure class="fig" id="beside-figure">
<img src={bands} width="540" height="180" alt="Three blue bands" />
<figcaption>A sized image inside a pinned figure.</figcaption>
</figure>
</div>
